## What this changes

What the app does now that it did not, or what it no longer does. Name the issue it
closes. Planning lives outside this repository, so the reasoning travels with the pull
request: what was decided and what the alternative cost. A decision that was not
obvious gets an ADR under `docs/adr/` and is linked here instead.

## Checks

`ci` runs these in `core` on Linux and in `platforms` on macOS and Windows, and
`privacy gate` runs the gate in `privacy`. Run them before you push:

- [ ] `cargo fmt -p satz-studio-core -p satz-studio -- --check` — the two packages, never `--all`
- [ ] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace --locked`
- [ ] `bash scripts/e2e.sh` — the verification harness, `docs/verification.md`
- [ ] `bash scripts/check-names.sh` — no customer, company or person, and no value outside satz's example table

## What this change also touches

Tick what applies, delete the rest:

- [ ] `README.md` and the page under `docs/` that describes what changed
- [ ] an ADR under `docs/adr/`
- [ ] `NOTICE` — a file bundled from elsewhere carries its line there
- [ ] `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md`, regenerated by `bash scripts/update-third-party-licenses.sh` because `Cargo.lock` moved
- [ ] the satz pin — the `vendor/satz` submodule, the recorded reports under `tests/fixtures` and the verbatim satz `NOTICE` copy move in one pull request, and `MIN_SATZ` stays where it is
- [ ] `MIN_SATZ` in `crates/satz-studio-core/src/satz/binary.rs`, because the app now uses something an older satz does not have — the test that needs it is named here

What to look at first, and what you are unsure about.
